lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: skills, training, and practice

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 4
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G4 Unit 2 — earning, work, and enterprise
objective: Learners compare invented pay rates before and after training, compute the weekly gain, and work out how many weeks it takes for the gain to cover the training cost.
scenario: Bianca is an invented fourth grader studying a pretend career board. An invented helper role pays $9.00 a simulated hour; after a $40.00 training course the same role pays $12.00 an hour. The board assumes 5 hours of work a week. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Work out a 5-hour week at Bianca's untrained rate of $9.00 an hour.

prompts.text: What does a 5-hour week pay before training?

tasks.directions: Now work out the same 5-hour week at the trained rate of $12.00 an hour, then find the weekly gain training buys.

prompts.text: What does a 5-hour week pay after training?
How much more does the trained week pay?

tasks.directions: The training cost $40.00 up front, and the weekly gain is the only thing paying it back.

prompts.text: How many whole weeks of the gain does it take to cover the $40.00 training?
After those weeks, how much more than the training cost has the gain produced?
Bianca's board shows training paying for itself in a few weeks. What would make that a worse deal than it looks?

remediation: Use the fictional scenario and work one graded prompt at a time. For each number response, copy the given fictional quantities into integer cents, choose the operation the wording calls for, calculate, and check the result with an inverse operation or estimate. For each written response, make a claim and support it with at least one detail from the fictional scenario. Use these steps to check the method while keeping every final result in your own response.
extension: Ask the learner what training cost would take exactly 4 weeks of the gain to repay, and to justify the figure.
